reason: The allowed interior transport regularity and classical Alexandrov estimates do not give differentiability at a boundary exposed point or remove the Monge–Ampere mass outside the target component. The authored proof must create centred sections whose one-dimensional endpoints straddle a hypothetical derivative jump, tune their forward length relative to their centre displacement, and contradict competing upper/lower volume estimates after normalization. It then uses the known Lipschitz singular interface to eliminate the outside-component Alexandrov mass and obtain local inverse-gradient regularity. This is a substantive boundary-localization argument beyond ordinary qualifying-exam estimates. I support H2 for this complete chain; no automatic H3 upgrade from the publication or theorem strength.
core_assessment:
exposed_point_localization: 381–477: compactness of the zero contact set, exposed-point localization and stability of nearby centred sections, with positive-height and zero-height limits treated separately. The omitted v(y_k) in463 tends to zero and does not alter either limit argument.
differentiability: 487–628: assume a one-sided derivative jump along an inward direction, use the balancing property and continuity in section height to arrange t2=t0/M, compare the near-minimum at p with its normalized boundary distance, and contradict lower/upper Alexandrov estimates. This entire bespoke argument remains a proof obligation.
local_Alexandrov_equation: 636–655: all subgradients in the local ball lie in the interior source; subgradients at points outside the convex target component can only land on the already known Lipschitz singular interface, so their image has zero Lebesgue measure.
final_regularization: 659–673: localized convex support and two-sided Alexandrov density justify the stated classical boundary power modulus; convex duality and the nonzero normal formula complete the local C1,beta conclusion. The source-local localization and differentiability are not supplied as prerequisites.

None supplies the current boundary exposed-point differentiability or outside-mass argument.
FK_specific_check: Independently read the primary Figalli–Kim author PDF, pp3–6: equation3.1, Proposition3.3 and Proposition3.4 with the adjacent discussion. The upper estimate requires a subgradient meeting a ball strictly inside the target; in the present application the target is the original source Omega and 0 is interior. Affine subtraction translates that same ball, so the constant stays independent of the chosen M. The interior strict-convexity implication used394/632 is the same cited Proposition3.4 (final numbering Proposition2), and should be named explicitly among allowed external facts.
FK_url: https://people.math.ethz.ch/~afigalli/papers-pdf/Partial-regularity-of-Brenier-solutions-of-the-Monge-Ampere-equation.pdf

standard_prerequisites.name: John normalization and standard centred-section properties
standard_prerequisites.statement: Centred convex sections exist, are dimensionally balanced, depend continuously on positive height, and satisfy the barrier estimate339.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localized Alexandrov estimates for Brenier solutions
standard_prerequisites.statement: Use la1/ua1 exactly as displayed365-374, with the upper estimate at a point whose subgradient meets an interior ball of the target. Constants may depend on the distance of that subgradient point to the target boundary. Also allow the same classical interior strict-convexity/differentiability result at a point inside the source whose subgradient meets the target interior, as invoked394 and632; this is Figalli-Kim Proposition3.4 in the author PDF (Proposition2 in the journal numbering).
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Figalli-Kim2010, author version Proposition3.3 and equation3.1, PDF pages3-6; the paper cites final numbering Proposition1/equation4. Exact hypotheses read at https://people.math.ethz.ch/~afigalli/papers-pdf/Partial-regularity-of-Brenier-solutions-of-the-Monge-Ampere-equation.pdf

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical localized boundary uniform convexity and convex duality
standard_prerequisites.statement: Once a convex support has two-sided Alexandrov density and uniformly localized centred sections near a boundary point, the local Caffarelli boundary method yields a power lower modulus for its gradient; Legendre duality gives Holder continuity of the inverse gradient.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: C96 Lemma2.2/Corollary2.3 and CM Theorem7.13, as invoked665-669. Applicability must be assessed; no local differentiability or localization lemma of the counted article is supplied freely.

core_obligations: Establish compactness of the dual contact set and locate exposed points on the separate target boundaries.
Prove uniform localization of centred sections near an exposed point despite the nonconvex source.
Rule out nondifferentiability by choosing a centred section with asymmetrically short outgoing segment, then contradicting upper and lower Alexandrov estimates.
Prove no extra Alexandrov mass is present outside the chosen target component near that point, then apply the classical boundary theorem and duality to obtain the claimed singular-set regularity.

proof_roadmap.step: Compact contact set and uniform centred-section localization.
Core boundary differentiability by delicate section choice and normalization.
Map unwanted subgradients into the measure-zero singular hypersurface.
Localized uniform convexity, Legendre duality and covering.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The classical background does not yield regularity at the interface because the source need not be convex. The counted author argument establishes the missing differentiability and local Alexandrov structure through exposed-point localization and a scale-selected asymmetric section contradiction. It is a substantive geometric-PDE mechanism; the short final invocation of a boundary theorem is not the entire proof.
